title: Chest X-ray for children
what: An X-ray of your child's chest. It shows the lungs and heart.
why: For a long-lasting cough, a high fever and possible pneumonia, or to check after treatment.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the report the same day
tell_doctor: If your child had a chest X-ray recently
If your child is scared, tell the technician. They will explain everything calmly
If the adult who will be there is pregnant, another adult should go

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: Tell your child ahead of time: there will be a big camera, it will not hurt, and they need to stand still and hold their breath.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A T-shirt with no metal prints or rhinestones. Take off necklaces and hair clips.

bring: Past chest X-rays, if you have them
A toy for a young child
steps: Your child undresses to the waist
Older children stand with their chest to the screen. Babies are imaged lying or sitting
You may be given a protective apron and asked to hold your child
Your child is asked to take a deep breath and hold it for a couple of seconds
The image takes a fraction of a second
feel: Babies sometimes cry because they are held. It is quick
after: Your child can get dressed and go home right away
Take the image and report to your pediatrician

faq.q: Is the radiation harmful for my child?
faq.a: The dose is very small. If your pediatrician ordered the X-ray, the benefit outweighs the risk.

faq.q: Can a parent stay in the room?
faq.a: Usually yes, in a protective apron. If you are pregnant, another adult should go.

reminders.text: Your child's chest X-ray is soon. Bring the referral and a favorite toy.
